text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Second round of talks between Greek Cypriot President Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Denktash starts on Monday in Montreux.
- Diplomats play down importance of agreement signed between north and Turkey last week on gradual integration.
- Montreux talks start with bad omens. Denktash demands that Cyprus put its EU membership application on hold and suspend purchase of S300 Russian anti-aircraft system.
- Prices commission set to look at increases in price of pork, beef and milk products.

- Diplomats optimistic the two leaders will sign agreement outlining commitment to open negotiations on Cyprus problem, but it will take a miracle to achieve progress on important issues related to dispute.
- Government will increase benefits and loans under self-employment scheme geared towards unemployed university graduates.
- Montreux talks start amid tension. Denktash says it will be the last if Clerides does not scrap S300 missile purchase and freeze Cyprus's EU application.
- Government will not take decision on liberalisation of interest rates because of presidential elections coming up in 1998.
